newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 2.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - March 2.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian cricketer Ian Healy faces possible suspension after throwing his bat following his dismissal during the third and final cricket Test in Pretoria, South Africa yesterday. The move signals the Australians' growing frustration at poor umpiring. Pae 18.

Australian Super League team, the Canberra Raiders, had poor season starting performances compounded upon by potentially serious injuries to back Ken Nagas and rugby union import Barry Lea in last night's 24-8 loss to Brisbane at ANZ Stadium. Page 18.

The New South Wales Supreme Court was told yesterday Australian boxer Kostya Tszyu was enticed by the greed of others when he turned on the man credited with establishing his career as an international superstar, Bill Mordey, in his defection from Mordey' boxing stable in 1995. Page 16.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Rugby League and South Queensland fullback Clinton Schifcofske revealed himself yesterday as the player under investigation by the Australian Sports Drug Agency after delivering an irregular sample. Page 48.

Australian golfer Stuart Appleby was narrowly defeated on Sunday in the A$1.91 million Bay Hill International, in his attempt to win two successive events on the US PGA Tour when he was beaten by American Phil Mickelson. Page 48.

For the first time international ironman competition, organisers of the upcoming World Oceanman Series have released the rankings of a field of competitors from three rival groups - Kellogg's, Uncle Toby's, and International Management Group. Page 47.
THE AGE

American professional surfer Kelly Slater has again been ranked number one for 1996 in the guide to the Rip Curl Pro which began at Winki Prop near Torquay in Victoria yesterday. The women's Quit Classic begins today. Page B6.

Australian tennis player Mark Philippoussis sped past ninth seed Wayne Ferreira to reach the fourth round of the $A3.1 million ATP Lipton championships yesterday, nearly breaking his own serving speed record of 224 kilometres and hour in the process. PageB6.

Australian Football League club Carlton is set to launch an international marketing campaign in a sponsorship of Australian sports journalist Frank Vardanega's radio reports. The reports will reach an estimated overseas audience of more than two million pople. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

The Australian Football League's move to the new Docklands Stadium looks set to delay the multi-million dollar plans to rebuild the Melbourne Cricket Ground's North Stand, with MCG secretary John Lill saying the $A350 million Victoria Stadium will have a egative impact on the MCG. Page 72.

Australian Sydney-based racehorse trainer Gai Waterhouse will fly back from Dubai on Friday to be at Randwick on Saturday for the $A1.1 million Doncaster Handicap. Waterhouse said "the Doncaster is my race and Randwick is my track." Page 65.

Australian marathon runner Steve Moneghetti placed 46th in the world cross-country championships in Turin , Italy yesterday - down on his 16th placing last year over the 12.3 kilometres. Moneghetti led the Australian team to 11th place. Page 64.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian Rugby League St George player Tony Hearn was last night cleared of making a high tackle on Illawarra forward Darren Bradstreet in Saturday's game at WIN Stadium. Hearn, who has a long suspension record, said he was "very relieved." Page 68.

Australian players Matthew Hayden, Matthew Elliott and Justin Langer look set to miss out on $A10,000 each after being replaced for the seven one-day matches that finish off the Australian cricket tour of South Africa. Page 68.

This weekend's Sail Sydney yacht racing regatta will mark the racing debut of the sponsorless Australian sailor and 2000 Olympics medal favourite Chris Nicholson and his crew Daniel Phillips. Page 65.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
